about.title: Dana Point Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Dana Point residents trust local clinics, urgent care centers, and nearby Orange County hospitals with some of the most important decisions of their lives — surgeries, diagnoses, childbirth, medication management. Most of the time, that trust is well placed. But when a provider misses a clear warning sign, operates on the wrong site, or fails to follow accepted medical standards, the consequences can be lasting. California's medical malpractice laws are notoriously technical, layered with strict notice requirements and shortened filing windows that don't match typical injury cases. A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't prove negligence occurred — proving malpractice requires expert medical review and a careful look at what a reasonably competent provider would have done differently. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your case ourselves. We simply listen to what happened and, if it seems appropriate, connect you with an independent California attorney experienced in these claims, free of charge and with no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney Early

items.title: Strict, Unforgiving Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to act — and a 90-day pre-suit notice must go out before a lawsuit is filed. Waiting even a few weeks can complicate a claim.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone doesn't establish malpractice, these claims typically need a qualified medical expert to explain how care fell below the accepted standard. An attorney can help arrange that kind of review.

items.title: Damages Caps Change Every Year
items.desc: California places a cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap adjusts annually by statute. Understanding how it applies to your situation is something an experienced attorney can walk you through.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Dana Point — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing. An independent attorney, often working with a medical expert, can help determine whether the facts support a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened. There's also a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement before filing, so it's wise to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney in Dana Point?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning they're paid only if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
